approved: Health Insurance Amendment (Extended Medicare Safety Net) Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would raise the general threshold of the Extended Medicare Safety Net to $2,000 from 1 January 2015.
It would also let the Chief Executive of Medicare decide how to contact families to confirm their composition, instead of requiring written requests.
The government says the measure would save $105.6 million over four years and not affect families receiving Family Tax Benefits Part A or concession card holders.
Increase the general EMSN threshold to $2,000.
Remove the requirement that family composition confirmation requests be in writing.
Individuals and families eligible for the Extended Medicare Safety Net, except those receiving Family Tax Benefits Part A or holding Commonwealth concession cards.

Said Labor would not block the bill raising the Extended Medicare Safety Net general threshold to $2,000 from 1 January 2015, since it originated in Labor's 2013 budget, but warned the Abbott government's further budget changes to the safety net would save $267 million over four years by giving patients less once they reach the threshold, and cited $24.8 billion in national out-of-pocket health spending in 2011 and 2012.
Referred the Health Insurance Amendment (Extended Medicare Safety Net) Bill 2014 and the Regulatory Powers (Standard Provisions) Bill 2014 to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

Supported the Health Insurance Amendment (Extended Medicare Safety Net) Bill 2014, which sets the general safety net threshold at $2,000 from 1 January 2015 and is projected to save $105.6 million, and described the Joondalup Health Campus and the new $20 million Shenton House cancer centre serving his Moore electorate.

Supported the Health Insurance Amendment (Extended Medicare Safety Net) Bill 2014 as an extension of a measure his own Labor government introduced in the 2013 to 2014 budget, citing Australian Institute of Health and Welfare figures showing out-of-pocket medical costs reached $24.8 billion in 2011 to 2012, and criticised the government's proposed $7 GP co-payment.

Defended the Health Insurance Amendment (Extended Medicare Safety Net) Bill 2014, saying about 11,000 Australians currently hit the $2,000 out-of-pocket threshold, and said the safety net, introduced in March 2004 by then health minister Tony Abbott, addresses moral hazard and provider leakage in the health system.

Supported the Health Insurance Amendment (Extended Medicare Safety Net) Bill 2014, noting it implements a measure from the previous Labor government's final budget projected to save $105.6 million, and accused the member for Shortland of hypocrisy for criticising a policy her own party introduced.

Criticised the government's claim of a health funding crisis, saying Medicare spending is actually 4.6 per cent of government outlays in 2013 to 2014, slightly down from a decade earlier, and said the Treasurer wrongly cited 11 average GP visits a year when the true figure is six.
